**A and B differ beyond the measured within-A sampling spread. The difference survives class balancing.** This is evidence about the reference distribution, not a generator score or an achievable FID floor.
ComparisonImages per setA subset vs BWithin A
Observed category mix3,020**21.14****14.92**
20 images per category3,020**20.83****14.80**
Values are medians over 20 seeds. Each seed draws disjoint U and V from A and compares FID(U,B) with FID(U,V); B stays fixed. Full, unequal-size **FID(A,B) = 15.71** is supplementary. Repeated subsampling variability is descriptive, not a confidence interval for model performance. ![Real-image FID: A/B versus within-A controls. The unique-pixel panel changes population and sample count; interpret it against its own baseline.](__FIG_fid_baselines__) **Implication for SiDA / DMD2.** Both methods combine teacher-derived signals with a real-image adversarial signal. Better matching the training distribution can coexist with a mismatch to B; increasing adversarial weight is therefore not an established cure for the reference shift. This is our inference from the EDA, not a result of a model ablation. Method context: [SiDA paper](https://proceedings.iclr.cc/paper_files/paper/2025/hash/ce953d71deeb33d9ffa2c879b518d273-Abstract-Conference.html), [DMD2 paper](https://papers.nips.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/hash/54dcf25318f9de5a7a01f0a4125c541e-Abstract-Conference.html). **How to use this result.** Keep the fixed A1/A2 development protocol, sample count, category schedule and export pipeline constant when comparing future recipes. Do not subtract 15.71 or the roughly six-point controlled gap from a generator FID; FID has no such additive decomposition. These baselines do not show that a model scoring near 20 has exhausted its improvement potential. Finite-sample FID bias is also model-dependent: [Chong & Forsyth](https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.07023). The strongest next direction is a small, controlled study of augmentation and coverage within A1/A2, with image quality and diversity checked alongside FID. EDA does not select a learning rate, loss weight, number of critic updates or augmentation probability.
Detailed base setup — shared by the EDA series **Scope and dates.** Dataset EDA completed on ; interpretation compiled on . No project generator or teacher was created, trained, tuned, sampled or evaluated. PCA and clustering are descriptive fits only. **Dataset.** [Kaggle Pokémon Generation One — 22k](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/bhawks/pokemon-generation-one-22k): 20,099 readable images across 151 categories. All listed images were present and decoded successfully.
PartitionImagesRole
A17,079Official training pool
A114,059Existing optimization subset
A23,020Existing development subset; 20/category
B3,020Official evaluation reference; 20/category
A1 and A2 are the existing immutable partition of A, copied from FastGen-SoFlow and verified byte-identical to the saved AFM and SiD-DiT partitions. A2 uses the existing seed-42, duplicate-aware selection; it is not an arbitrary fresh random holdout. No split was regenerated. These checks do not establish that every teammate's separate run used that same partition. **Image path.** Supplied white compositing for transparency → RGB → supplied bilinear 64 × 64 resize → tensor normalization and official uint8 PNG export round-trip → clean-fid clean-mode float bicubic 299 × 299 resize. EDA therefore describes what the official 64 × 64 pipeline retains, not all native-resolution detail. Thirty verification images, including all six non-RGB sources, matched the supplied export pixel-for-pixel and the clean-fid loader tensor-for-tensor. **Representation.** Frozen standard clean-fid Inception-v3 features, 2,048 dimensions; no learned project checkpoint. FID uses full unnormalized features and float64 statistics. The numerical implementation agreed with clean-fid on full A/B to about 1.5e-12; B/B self-FID was zero. PCA is fitted on A only; cluster centers are fitted on A only; B uses those fixed transforms. Full A includes development A2 for dataset description, not model training. **Sampling controls.** Twenty predefined seeds, 20261005–20261024; each regular set contains 3,020 images. Uniform sampling preserves A's observed category mixture in expectation; the balanced control takes 20 per category in each subset. Exact duplicates are retained in the main analysis and addressed separately in [EDA-7](__EDA_7__). **Environment and integrity.** Independent Conda copy aligned with FastGen-SoFlow: Python 3.10.21, torch 2.7.1+cu126, torchvision 0.22.1+cu126, clean-fid 0.1.35, NumPy 1.26.4, SciPy 1.15.3; scikit-learn 1.7.2 added for EDA. Feature extraction used GPU 0. Original files and split manifests passed hash checks; sibling projects were unchanged. **Boundary for later tuning.** B has been inspected for this descriptive audit. Do not use B images, B-derived cluster weights/background targets, or repeated B scores to choose training settings. Select on A2 and disclose this EDA exposure when describing B as held out. The supplied README reserves B for evaluation and permits hyperparameter selection only within A. **Current team context.** The SiDA log describes a development holdout, while the DMD2 log describes train-split FID selection. Before comparing methods, reconcile the reference split/hash, sample count and generation protocol. The EDA does not independently verify the reported frontier ranking. **Local provenance.** `/home/user/jw_soflow/exploration/eda/REPORT.md`, `eda/features/metadata.json`, `eda/resources/provenance.json`, and `eda/reports/analysis/validation.json`. These are local artifact identifiers, not web links.
Other methodology reports - [EDA-2 — PCA: directions of visual variation](__EDA_2__) - [EDA-3 — Nearest neighbors: individual coverage](__EDA_3__) - [EDA-4 — Clusters: mode proportions](__EDA_4__) - [EDA-5 — Split ordering and metadata](__EDA_5__) - [EDA-6 — Image properties and augmentation hypotheses](__EDA_6__) - [EDA-7 — Duplicate overlap and sensitivity](__EDA_7__)

properties.Title: EDA-2 — PCA directions of visual variation

content:
Shared setup: fixed A/A1/A2/B partitions and official 64 × 64 image preparation, using frozen Inception features; see [EDA-1 — detailed base setup](__EDA_1__).

**B shifts along several major feature directions; brightness and illustration style are prominent, but not the whole explanation.**

**Method.** Principal component analysis (PCA) finds directions of greatest variation in A's image features. We project both datasets onto the same centered, unwhitened basis and compare their distributions. This shows *where* they differ; components are not predefined semantic labels.

- PC2 has the largest mean shift among the first ten PCs: **+0.417 A standard deviations** for B.
- PC2 correlates with brightness within A (**0.529**) and B (**0.553**, Spearman). Its low-end examples include scenic/card artwork; high-end examples include isolated characters on bright backgrounds.
- The first two PCs explain only **9.26%** of A's variance. Overlapping points in this scatter do not imply equivalent distributions.

![A and B projected onto A-fitted PCs. Equal-size display samples; the plotted axes capture only a small part of total variation.](__FIG_pca_scatter__)

**Generative-model implication.** A single global FID can conceal whether a change affects style, background, color or subject appearance. These directions provide a compact diagnostic vocabulary for a later, separately authorized comparison of generated samples with A2. They are not evidence that the current SiDA or DMD2 output has any particular defect.

**Guidance.** Treat brightness/color augmentation as a distribution-changing intervention that needs inspection at 64 × 64. Do not optimize a model toward B's PC2 mean or declare a PC to be a pure “quality” axis. Inspect whole characters and within-class diversity as well as aggregate feature shifts.

<details>
<summary>Per-PC distributions and visual anchors</summary>
	![Distributions of the first ten A-fitted components. Signs are arbitrary and refer to the saved basis.](__FIG_pca_distributions__)

	![Low and high extremes of the first four PCs; original-aspect thumbnail beside actual 64 × 64 input. Endpoint examples illustrate an axis, not its exclusive meaning.](__FIG_pca_endpoints__)

	The first 64 PCs explain 58.66% of A's variance. Other components mix identity, pose, texture and color. PCA captures linear variation in this one representation; it is neither a complete semantic map nor a causal explanation.
</details>

properties.Title: EDA-3 — Nearest neighbors and individual coverage

content:
Shared setup: fixed A/A1/A2/B partitions and official 64 × 64 image preparation, using full 2,048-dimensional Inception features; see [EDA-1 — detailed base setup](__EDA_1__). **B is not globally more isolated from A. Distribution shift here does not primarily mean every B image lacks a training analogue.** **Method.** For each B image, find the closest A image by Euclidean feature distance. Large distances identify candidates for visual coverage review. Compare held-out A and B against the *same* A gallery so gallery size does not determine the conclusion.
MeasureResult
B → all A: median / 95th percentile8.82 / 13.80
B queries with exact matches in A343 / 3,020 (11.36%)
Median excluding those exact-matched B queries9.60
Nearest A image has the same Pokémon category82.42%
Same-gallery comparison, 20 repeatsB median lower than held-out A in all 20
![Nearest-neighbor distance distributions. Use the common-gallery controls for comparisons; raw reverse A→B has a smaller gallery.](__FIG_neighbor_distributions__) **What the tail shows.** Unusual sprites, cards and crops appear among the distant examples. Some contain recognizable artwork already in A under another framing. In the Marowak example below, a large distance coexists with visibly shared artwork. Feature distance is not proof of novel content or a missing semantic mode.
Selected high-distance examples ![Tail ranks 1–8. Each B query is followed by its three closest A images; each cell includes the native-aspect and 64 × 64 views.](__FIG_neighbor_tail_1__) ![Tail ranks 17–24. The first Marowak row illustrates a framing-sensitive large distance despite recognizable shared artwork.](__FIG_neighbor_tail_3__)
**Generative-model implication.** Improving sharpness alone and discovering missing modes are different problems. The current evidence makes mode proportions and variation within familiar modes important hypotheses; it does not exclude difficult rare cases. For future augmentation design, modest framing robustness is worth testing inside A1/A2, but aggressive crops can remove the Pokémon or create an unintended target distribution. **Limit.** This is real-to-real coverage, not generated-sample precision/recall, diversity or memorization measurement. Exact duplicates affect the result. A-fitted feature distance may emphasize color or composition over class identity; review the images before interpreting any tail sample.

properties.Title: EDA-4 — Cluster composition and mode proportions

content:
Shared setup: fixed A/A1/A2/B partitions and official 64 × 64 image preparation, using the first 64 A-fitted PCs; see [EDA-1 — detailed base setup](__EDA_1__). **The strongest discrepancy is how often visual modes occur. Balancing Pokémon categories barely changes it.** **Method.** K-means groups A images into 32 feature-space clusters; B is assigned to the same centers. Comparing each cluster's share, p_A(k) versus p_B(k), reveals over- and underrepresented visual modes. Names below are tentative descriptions from representative images, not ground-truth style labels.
Illustrative clusterA shareB shareB − A
19: isolated orange/tan illustrations4.16%11.39%+7.23 pp
2: isolated blue/pale illustrations3.52%8.44%+4.92 pp
9: scenic/action artwork3.31%1.03%−2.28 pp
3: toys/plush photographs and some renders4.75%2.68%−2.07 pp
![Shares of A and B in the same 32 A-fitted feature clusters.](__FIG_cluster_composition__) Cluster total variation, half the sum of absolute share differences, is **0.261**; with equal category weighting it is **0.260**. The median between two balanced A subsets is **0.055**. TV summarizes a shift in cluster proportions; 0.261 does not mean 26.1% of B contains missing content. Sensitivity runs at 16 and 64 clusters retain substantial shifts (0.235 and 0.270). **Generative-model implication.** Class-balanced generation can still miss the *within-class style mixture*. A model may depict all 151 categories and still overproduce one pose, rendering type or background. Stronger adversarial matching to A1 does not automatically correct the mismatch to B. **Guidance.** In later authorized model work, inspect generated mode occupancy and within-class variety against A2 alongside FID. A lower FID accompanied by fewer visual modes should prompt review. Do not set training weights to p_B(k), remove scenic images to mimic B, or treat these unsupervised groups as class labels.
Representative images and limits ![Cluster 19, enriched in B. Three central and two more distant distinct-image representatives per split row.](__FIG_cluster_01_k32_19__) ![Cluster 9, depleted in B. Examples emphasize scenic/action artwork.](__FIG_cluster_05_k32_9__) ![Cluster 3, depleted in B. Photographs of physical objects are visible alongside some rendered images.](__FIG_cluster_06_k32_3__) The retained PCs explain 58.66% of A variance. Assigning B to A's centers can hide a B-only mode. Cluster descriptors are visual interpretations, not exhaustive annotations or a formal mode-collapse test.

properties.Title: EDA-5 — Split ordering and metadata audit

content:
Shared setup: fixed A/A1/A2/B partitions and official 64 × 64 image preparation; see [EDA-1 — detailed base setup](__EDA_1__). **B has an exact filename-order signature. It should not be interpreted as an ordinary random holdout from A's mixture.** **Method.** Audit the fixed manifests, category counts, lexicographic filename ranks, file formats and native image sizes. This detects observable selection structure without fitting a model or inferring undocumented image provenance. - In **all 151 categories**, B equals exactly the **first 20 lexicographically sorted filenames** in the combined A∪B list for that category. - A contains **46–183 images per category**; B contains **20 each**. A1 contains **26–163 per category**. - PNG share is **0.86% in A versus 44.24% in B**. Median native dimensions are **436 × 435 in A versus 200 × 200 in B** (separate width/height medians).
Observable factInterpretation
Lexicographic first-20 pattern in every categoryStrong evidence of structured selection; historical split code was not reviewed.
Format and size differ substantiallyPossible collection/style associations; metadata alone does not establish source provenance.
Category balancing leaves the FID gapCategory frequency alone is insufficient to explain the visual shift.
**Generative-model implication.** A student and teacher trained only within A can learn a different visual mixture from the fixed FID reference. A2 remains the required development set, but success on A2 is not a guarantee of the same gain on B. This is a dataset property shared by methods; it cannot explain the SiDA–DMD2 ranking on its own. **Guidance.** Keep all partitions fixed. Use the official 20-per-category generation schedule for comparable reporting, and consider class-balanced A1 sampling as an A2-tested design choice—not a remedy for the entire shift. Avoid selecting “early” filenames or PNG-only training samples to reproduce B. There is no evidence here for converting files, lowering resolution or changing the official loader. **Limit.** The ordering pattern is exact; its causal responsibility for style differences is a plausible interpretation, not proven historical attribution. The EDA does not establish any challenge-rule change or permission to tune against B.

properties.Title: EDA-6 — Image properties and augmentation hypotheses

content:
Shared setup: fixed A/A1/A2/B partitions and official 64 × 64 image preparation; see [EDA-1 — detailed base setup](__EDA_1__). **Brightness and near-white pixels differ strongly, even within every Pokémon category. Augmentation should preserve useful variation rather than force images toward B's appearance.** **Method.** Measure simple properties on the actual 64 × 64 RGB inputs: near-white pixel fraction, brightness, saturation and edge/texture summaries. These interpretable measurements complement Inception features and help identify what an augmentation would change.
Per-image statistic (median)AB
Near-white pixel fraction0.29%37.52%
Brightness, 0–1 scale0.6150.762
Saturation, 0–1 scale0.2790.207
B's median near-white fraction is higher in **all 151 categories**. Near-white means all three RGB channels exceed 0.95; this is not a background segmentation or an estimate of subject size. ![Distributions of measured 64 × 64 input properties. Near-white pixels may include both subject and background.](__FIG_image_properties__) **Implication for adversarial distillation.** A discriminator could exploit background, framing or color cues, but this EDA does not show that the current SiDA/DMD2 discriminators do so. Distinguish two interventions: modifying the real-image distribution used by a teacher changes its learning target; augmenting discriminator inputs aims to regularize the real/fake comparison.
Candidate for a future A1/A2 ablationWhat to check before expecting a benefit
Small translations or mild scale changesCharacter remains complete at 64 × 64; padding introduces no artificial border cue.
Horizontal flips where semantically acceptableInspect text/cards and asymmetry; establish whether the current recipe already uses flips.
Mild brightness/saturation changesPreserve species cues and style diversity; color invariance is not automatically desirable.
Aggressive crop, cutout, background removal/replacementLower-priority, higher target-distortion risk; requires separate evidence from A.
For a DiffAugment-style adversarial branch, use the same augmentation policy/distribution on real and generated inputs and preserve gradients through the generated-image transform. This does not require pairing identical random transforms between unrelated images. Its effectiveness in standalone GANs is motivation, not evidence of a gain in these distillation implementations. [DiffAugment paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.10738). **Guidance.** Keep an unaugmented control and vary one augmentation family/strength at a time, selecting on A2. Do not automatically apply image transforms to teacher or fake-score regression targets: coordinate transforms, noise/time conditioning and targets must remain mathematically consistent. Do not whiten backgrounds, remove scenic images, or choose augmentation strength to hit B's 37.52% statistic. These are hypotheses for later work; no augmentation experiment was run.

properties.Title: EDA-7 — Exact duplicate overlap and FID sensitivity

content:
Shared setup: fixed A/A1/A2/B partitions and official 64 × 64 image preparation; see [EDA-1 — detailed base setup](__EDA_1__). **The evaluation reference contains exact training-pool matches, yet the A/B shift persists when those matches are excluded. Coverage and generalization need separate interpretations.** **Method.** Hash file bytes and decoded RGB pixels, including the actual 64 × 64 inputs. Identical hashes flag exact content sharing; a second, explicitly changed-population FID analysis tests whether the shift persists without it. - **343 of 3,020 B images (11.36%)** have exact matches in A, confirmed at both native RGB and 64 × 64 RGB levels. - Across the full dataset, **1,416 RGB duplicate groups** contain **1,421 redundant files**. - There are **no exact RGB duplicate groups crossing A1/A2**. This does not rule out near-duplicate artwork with different crops, compression or borders.
Unique-pixel sensitivity: 2,677 images/set, 20 seedsMedian FID
Unique A subset vs B with A-matching groups excluded**24.66**
Within A, disjoint unique-pixel groups**16.81**
The sensitivity keeps one representative per 64 × 64 RGB group and prevents content sharing between its two A subsets. It changes B and sample count, so compare **24.66 with 16.81 within this scheme**; the difference from the main 3,020-image score is not a quantified “duplicate penalty.” **Generative-model implication.** Memorizing some A images could reproduce part of B's reference content; this audit establishes that possibility, not that any current model memorizes. Low reference FID alone therefore cannot establish novel-image generation. Duplicates also increase the effective sampling frequency of certain artworks, which matters in small-data adversarial training. **Guidance.** Preserve the official data and score. In later authorized work, inspect generated-to-A1 neighbors and within-class diversity, and build a perceptual near-duplicate-family audit within A for a supplementary generalization check. Any duplicate-aware sampler is a separate A2-tested intervention, not an automatic cleanup. Do not remove examples because they happen to match B. **Connection to development results.** A2's duplicate-aware construction makes it structurally different from B. That helps explain why A2 and B can give different coverage impressions, but it does not predict a direction or numerical offset for model FID. See [EDA-3 — nearest-neighbor controls](__EDA_3__) and [EDA-1 — main FID controls](__EDA_1__).
